title: Body Louse: Just a Head Louse in Disguise?
description: Many think body lice diverged from head lice over 100,000 years ago. New genetic studies reveal they are almost identical, differing only by regulatory shifts that let them live in clothing. The supposed ancient split is now questioned.
narration: BODY LOUSE IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You assume the body louse split from head lice centuries ago as a separate species. Actually it’s just a head louse that moved to clothing via regulatory changes recently. Recent transcriptome analyses show body and head lice are almost genetically identical, suggesting significant phenotypic flexibility from regulatory, possibly epigenetic, changes rather than long‑term divergence. The earlier estimate of a 107,000‑year split used to date clothing adoption is now questioned. So the body louse is simply a head louse in adaptation.
